mintAuthority.summary: MUSD is minted on Mezo through the Liquity-style CDP route (BorrowerOperations opens troves against BTC at a 110% minimum collateral ratio; InterestRateManager mints accrued interest), with the mintList allowlist administered by the Mezo protocol owner, a 5-of-9 Safe that owns the token contract on Mezo, Ethereum, and Base. On Ethereum and Base the only mint authority besides that owner Safe is the Wormhole NTT manager (burning spoke), which mints against guardian-attested cross-chain messages.

controls.label: Mezo BorrowerOperations CDP mint route
controls.capDescription: BorrowerOperations mints MUSD only against troves collateralized by BTC at or above the 110% minimum collateral ratio; the InterestRateManager 0x4a453700d157717Fe02fB62E7700ED7845048285 is the second system minter for accrued interest. No separate cap-raising authority exists for this route.
controls.evidence: At Mezo block 10534345 (2026-07-20, https://jsonrpc-mezo.boar.network): mintList(0x44b1bac67dDA612a41a58AAf779143B181dEe031) = true and mintList(InterestRateManager 0x4a453700d157717Fe02fB62E7700ED7845048285) = true on the MUSD token. The pinned MUSD.sol source shows mint() requires mintList[msg.sender] and the Liquity system contracts are the CDP mint route; minting is economically bounded by BTC collateral at the 110% MCR, not by a supply cap.

controls.label: Mezo protocol owner Safe (MUSD token owner on Mezo, Ethereum, Base)
controls.capDescription: The owner Safe administers the token's mintList/burnList allowlists (addToMintList/addToBurnList are onlyOwner in MUSD.sol) on all three deployments, so it can authorize arbitrary new minters; it does not itself call mint().
controls.evidence: At Ethereum block 25571115 (2026-07-20): owner() of the MUSD token = 0x98D8899c3030741925BE630C710A98B57F397C7a on Ethereum, Base, and Mezo; the address is a 171-byte Safe proxy whose getThreshold() = 5 and getOwners() returns the 9 listed addresses. The same Safe address carries bytecode on Mezo (block 10534345). Through onlyOwner addToMintList it controls who may mint on every chain.

controls.label: Wormhole NTT manager (Ethereum burning spoke)
controls.capDescription: The NTT manager mints MUSD on Ethereum only against guardian-attested NTT burn messages from Mezo/Base (Wormhole NTT v1.1.0 burning mode, transceiver threshold 1); NTT per-chain inbound rate limits apply but reset and are not a supply cap.
controls.evidence: An eth_getLogs scan for MintListAddressAdded on the MUSD token from its Ethereum deployment block 22467780 through 25571115 returned exactly one event, at block 22973966, adding 0x5293158bf7a81ED05418DA497a80F7e6DBF4477E; at block 25571115 mintList(manager) = true. The 209-byte proxy manager reads token() = MUSD and mode() = 1 (burning), matching the issuer's ntt-bridge-musd-mainnet deployment.json. It is the sole non-owner minter on Ethereum.

controls.label: Wormhole NTT manager (Base burning spoke)
controls.capDescription: The NTT manager mints MUSD on Base only against guardian-attested NTT burn messages from Mezo/Ethereum (Wormhole NTT v1.1.0 burning mode, transceiver threshold 1); NTT per-chain inbound rate limits apply but reset and are not a supply cap.
controls.evidence: At Base block 48863636 (2026-07-20): mintList(0x3EB418BdBE95b4b9cf465ecfBD8424685ACD1Bc1) = true on the MUSD token; the 209-byte proxy manager reads token() = MUSD and mode() = 1 (burning), matching the issuer's ntt-bridge-musd-mainnet deployment.json for the Base burning spoke.

review.evidence: 2026-07-20 on-chain review across Mezo, Ethereum, and Base. The MUSD token (same 6,436-byte deployment at 0xdd468a1ddc392dcdbef6db6e34e89aa338f9f186 on all three chains) gates mint() through an owner-administered mintList. On Mezo (block 10534345) the minters are the Liquity system contracts BorrowerOperations and InterestRateManager — the user-collateralized CDP route bounded by the 110% BTC MCR. The token owner on all three chains is the 5-of-9 Safe 0x98D8899c3030741925BE630C710A98B57F397C7a (threshold/owners read at Ethereum block 25571115). On Ethereum a full MintListAddressAdded log scan from the deployment block 22467780 through 25571115 returned exactly one allowlist addition: the Wormhole NTT manager 0x5293158bf7a81ED05418DA497a80F7e6DBF4477E (block 22973966), which reads token()=MUSD and mode()=1 (burning). On Base (block 48863636) mintList holds for the NTT manager 0x3EB418BdBE95b4b9cf465ecfBD8424685ACD1Bc1 (mode()=1 burning). Both managers match the issuer's ntt-bridge-musd-mainnet deployment.json; the Mezo hub manager 0x7efb386675d75280D39Aae42964A6776DE0ee0bD reads mode()=0 (locking) and holds the locked bridged-out supply. No LayerZero endpoint() surface exists on any deployment. No supply cap is encoded anywhere; economically the CDP route is bounded by BTC collateral inflows and the NTT spokes by guardian-attested burns, so the profile records unbounded economic cap semantics. Upgrade-authority check (2026-07-21): at Ethereum block 25579960, Base block 48983502, and Mezo block 10555283, the MUSD token's EIP-1967 implementation, admin, and beacon storage slots all read zero on every chain, and its runtime code is 6,436 bytes (the full contract, not a thin proxy); MUSD is therefore an immutable, non-upgradeable deployment, so the owner Safe's mintList/burnList administration described above is the entire privileged surface with no separate implementation-upgrade path. Economic-posture fields reviewed 2026-08-15: the owner Safe can install arbitrary minters, so ActivePool and bridge accounting do not reconcile every possible mint path and no prudential supervisor is named. Wave 2 external review 2026-08-15: Mezo's architecture, bridge deployment, and audit pages document the CDP, NTT, and security-audit surfaces but provide no independent whole-supply reconciliation that also constrains an owner-added minter.
